findings.summary: The 8-word 'new' window contradicts the plan's own test and exempts the very reliance phrasing the check exists to catch.
findings.evidence: Decision 3 says a candidate is exempt when a 'new' word (new, add, adds, ...) appears before it in the same clause, at most 8 words back. In 'adds X beside Y', 'adds' is 3 words before Y, in the same clause, so Y is exempt under that rule. Yet the criterion 2 demonstration asserts that an absent Y is refused. Either the test fails or the rule is not what the plan describes. The design also has a soundness gap. A failing reading usually says 'adds a new X, reusing Y' or 'adds X beside Y from job Z'. With an 8-word look-back, every name in that clause that the reading relies on is exempted by the earlier 'adds', so Part 2 is silently switched off in exactly that case. Words such as 'add' and 'create' are also very common in survey prose, so the exemption fires far more widely than intended. Fix: Make the exemption apply only to what the marker introduces, not to every name after it in the clause. Simplest option: exempt only the first candidate after a marker word within the window. Stop the window at relation words such as beside, reusing, using, calls, extends, from, with, next to, after and before, so 'adds X beside Y' exempts X and still checks Y. State the rule in decision 3 and D146, and keep the 'adds X beside Y' case and an 'adds a new X, reusing Y' case as tests.
findings.location: Plan decision 3 ('new' exemption window); Demonstration for criterion 2, case 'adds X beside Y passes X and refuses an absent Y'

findings.summary: Part 1 refuses any prose path missing from the snapshot, which goes beyond the reading's subject (relying on an earlier job's unlanded files). This will catch historical mentions and paths that refused examples cite.
findings.evidence: The reading says the check refuses 'a reading relying on an earlier job's or path's unlanded files' and that 'Part 3 starts only from jobs, paths or file stems the reading's own text names'. Part 1 instead checks every path token in the title, summary, departures, assumptions and criteria with no notion of reliance. A sentence such as 'D119 removed crates/x/old.rs' is refused until it gets an out_of_scope entry. The plan accepts this and names out_of_scope as the repair, but each such refusal uses up the reader's one correction. Fix: Either limit Part 1 to assumptions and summary (where a reading claims something exists), or skip path tokens in a clause that names a removal or past state (removed, deleted, was, formerly). Otherwise keep it as is, but state in D146 that this is wider than reliance and why.
findings.location: Plan decision 6 / Part 1 (path tokens anywhere in prose)

findings.summary: String literals and test fixtures count as existing code, so a name in a test string or in this change's own fixtures can make a planned name exist.
findings.evidence: The plan admits this gap and mitigates it by building fixture names from pieces. But the snapshot already contains many test modules whose string fixtures hold function-like names (for example the readings in reading.rs tests), and any of them counts as existing. This only lowers refusals, so it is safe, but the class coverage claimed for criterion 2 is weaker than stated. Fix: Optionally skip lines inside `#[cfg(test)]` modules or files named *_tests.rs / tests.rs when building the corpus. At least list this in D146 as a known gap alongside block comments.
findings.location: Plan decision 4 (corpus = whole-word match on non-comment .rs lines)

findings.evidence: 'an unlanded `docs/design~-cause.md`' should presumably be `docs/design~-cause.md` or similar. Fix: Use the intended path, for example `docs/design~-cause.md`.

summary: The plan is grounded in the code. I read reading.rs and athena-git/src/lib.rs, and every function it names exists: read_once at 372, check_reading_acceptance at 2678, check_boundary_and_repo_files at 2600, referenced_jobs at 2335, unaccounted_files at 2472, names_path_token at 2516, code_surveys at 2917, carry, job_ids_in and replay_declaration, plus Git::cat_blobs and ls_tree in athena-git. The survey symbols check_record_file and AnyRecord exist in athena-data/src/records.rs. Chaining the new check after check_reading_acceptance inside read_once (lines 520-529) keeps the reader's one correction and avoids churning about 45 call sites; the plan states this departure from the brief's wording and proves the wiring with the reader-level test. Part 3 starts only from what the reading's own text names, which answers the earlier over-refusal finding, and the demonstrations call the production functions through real seams. One design fault needs fixing before production. The 8-word 'new' exemption window covers every name after an 'adds' or 'new' in the clause. That contradicts the plan's own criterion 2 case ('adds X beside Y' refuses an absent Y), and it switches off the symbol check in the usual reliance phrasing ('adds X, reusing Y'). Narrow the exemption to what the marker introduces. The other findings are minor: Part 1 goes wider than reliance, string literals and test fixtures count as existing code, and a fixture path in the criterion 5 test is garbled.
